Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

capture verb

a person or an animal

also catch, take captive, be captured, capture alive, trap

classical

Plaut. Rud. 2.1.12: neque quicquam captum'st piscium (Lewis & Short)
Ov. A.A. 1.763

capiō, capere, cēpī, captum

verb, third conjugation

catch, take, capture

Of people taken in war (captī, captives) and of animals, birds and fish caught. A captive is captīvus (see prisoner).

Other words

  • comprehendō, comprehendere, comprehendī, comprehēnsum — seize, arrest

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical

    Of a wanted person, a thief, a runaway: see arrest.

  • prēndō (prehendō), prēndere, prēndī, prēnsum — grab, catch hold of

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.22.1: mustēla ab homine prēnsa

    To lay hold of with the hand: a person by the arm, an animal by the scruff.

Examples

  • mustēla ab homine prēnsa cum īnstantem necem effugere vellet: parce, quaesō, inquit, mihi

    a weasel caught by a man, wanting to escape the death that was coming: “spare me, please,” she saidPhaedr. 1.22.1–3

  • vēnor aliquandō, sed nōn sine pugillāribus, ut quamvīs nihil cēperim nōn nihil referam

    I hunt sometimes, but not without my notebooks, so that even if I catch nothing I bring something backPlin. Ep. 9.36.6

See also capture, arrest, prisoner, hunt, catch with a hook, escape.
